newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge refuses to delay Reynolds trial.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge refuses to delay Reynolds trial.

text.p: A Florida judge has refused to postpone product liability case against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, which last month won a trial brought by the same attorney who is representing the current plaintiff.

Reynolds attorneys said at a pretrial conference Tuesday that they needed more time to prepare for an August 4 trial in a lawsuit filed on behalf of Joann Karbiwnyk, a former smoker who contracted lung cancer.
But Circuit Judge Michael Weatherby said the trial date had already been moved from June to August and he was not inclined to make further delays.

The plaintiff's attorney, Norwood "Woody" Wilner, who has filed hundreds of lawsuits against tobacco companies on behalf of smokers, urged the judge to adhere to the schedule. Wilner said he had another case against a cigarette maker scheduled for trial in November.
Karbiwnyk, whose lung cancer has spread to her brain, might not live to testify if the trial were moved to October, lawyers said.

Karbiwnyk, 49, smoked Reynolds brand cigarettes until she quit in 1984. Her cancer was diagnosed about a decade later. Reynolds, the country's second-largest cigarette maker, is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
Reynolds attorney Jim Young said the defense team needed more time to question Wilner's expert witnesses. "We simply aren't in a position to try the case in six weeks," he said.
Wilner sued on counts of negligence, including failure to warn consumers about the product's dangers and liability, including claims that Reynolds cigarettes were defective.
Wilner will ask the judge for permission to seek punitive damages from Reynolds in the Karbiwnyk case.

The $368.5 billion agreement between the tobacco industry and state attorneys general would prohibit punitive damages for individual plaintiffs. But the pact has not been approved by Congress and was unlikely to be a done-deal by the trial.
Wilner sought punitive damages in the earlier case against Reynolds, but jurors did not find the company at fault for her cancer.

He did not ask for punitive damages in his 1996 case against Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp., in which a Jacksonville jury awarded $750,000 to his client, former smoker Grady Carter. The judgment is being appealed. Brown & Williamson is a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc.
